description: Former US Ambassador to Israel under the Biden administration Thomas Nides calls Iran’s regime “dangerous” and says he hopes the US and Israel are aligned in their objectives in the region. He also argues lasting change must come from the Iranian people, not imposed from the top down. He speaks on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Change Must Come From ‘Bottom Up’: Nides

author: Carla Samon Ros
description: Peru’s president appointed Luis Arroyo as prime minister on Tuesday, the third cabinet chief named in a month in the politically-turbulent nation.
title: Peru’s New President Names His Third Prime Minister in a Month

author: Golnar Motevalli
description: Iran confirmed the death of Ali Larijani, the Islamic Republic’s national security chief and a key figure in its wartime leadership, after Israel announced earlier that it had killed him in an overnight airstrike.
title: Iran Confirms Security Chief Larijani Killed in Israeli Strike

author: Anthony Capaccio, Courtney McBride
description: The USS Gerald R. Ford aircraft carrier is leaving the fight with Iran and heading back to port, a US official familiar with the matter said, after a fire broke out in its laundry area and left at least two sailors with non-life-threatening injuries.
title: US Carrier Involved in Iran Fight Heads Back to Port After Fire

author: Jen Judson
description: The Pentagon is planning to mass produce one-way LUCAS attack drones, which have been deployed by US forces in the current war in the Middle East after they were created by reverse-engineering Iran’s cheap and deadly Shahed system.
title: Pentagon Plans to Mass Produce Attack Drone Used in Iran War

author: Antonia Mufarech
description: Chile’s new government moved to withdraw dozens of environmental decrees issued under the previous administration, a sweeping move that threatens to damage the Latin American nation’s green credentials as it looks to boost investment.
title: Chile’s Kast Halts Green Decrees in Rush to Undo Boric Legacy

author: Jonnelle Marte
description: Economists debate whether the economy is increasingly relying on spending by the rich.
title: Has the K-Shaped Consumer Spending Story Been Exaggerated?

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: Hawaii’s long-awaited plans to import natural gas — and burn it to produce electricity — are advancing, with Japan’s largest power-generation company laying out a blueprint for development over the next five years.
title: Hawaii’s Gas Bid Advances on Japan Plan for Power Plant, Imports

author: Allyson Versprille
description: Federal airport security screeners on Monday called out of work at the highest rate since the partial government shutdown affecting the Department of Homeland Security began more than a month ago.
title: One in Ten Airport Screeners Skip Work as Funding Fight Drags On

author: Eric Martin, Patricia Garip, Peter Millard, Fabiola Zerpa
description: The Trump administration intends to take additional steps to ease sanctions on Venezuela’s oil sector in an effort to increase crude production as the Iran war sends prices surging.
title: US to Ease Venezuela Sanctions to Unlock More Oil Amid Iran War

author: Anthony Capaccio, Jen Judson
description: The US military official leading the effort to build the Golden Dome missile-defense shield put a $185 billion price tag on the first stage of the project, a $10 billion cost increase that highlights the project’s massive — and imprecise — ambitions.
title: US Official Leading Golden Dome Raises Price by $10 Billion

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Bloomberg Middle East reporter Dan Williams on Israel's goals for the war with Iran after it took out a top Iranian leader Tuesday. Then, Alex Vatanka, senior fellow at the Middle East Institute, discusses what a post-war future looks like for Iran and what kind of threat the country really posed to the United States and its allies. Plus, Ellen Wald, founder of Transversal Consulting & Atlantic Council senior fellow, talks energy interdependence and President Trump's claims that oil prices will drop back down after the war is over. Finally, Bloomberg's Monique Mulima and Paige Smith break down how bitcoin has become a safe haven during a period of global turmoil and why Mastercard chose this moment to buy stablecoin firm BVNK. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Bashes NATO Allies as Iran War Intensifies, Oil Rises | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/17/2026

description:
Trump scolded North Atlantic Treaty Organization allies in particular, denouncing their “foolish mistake” in not joining the US effort and claiming none in the group posed reservations at the start of the war, which the president has long claimed was needed to remove a potent nuclear threat. 
“I’ve long said I wonder whether or not NATO would ever be there for us,” Trump said Tuesday at the White House. “This was a great test because we don’t need them, but they should have been there.” President Trump says NATO is making a foolish mistake. Trump spoke at the White House White House at a Bilateral meeting with Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin Trump added that the US didn’t have to be there for Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: NATO Is Making a Foolish Mistake Says Trump (Full Q&A)

author: Ella Feldman, Lucia Kassai
description: A tanker carrying Russian crude appears headed to Cuba as the fuel-starved Caribbean island seeks a reprieve three months after the Trump administration effectively shut off the flow of oil to the country.
title: Cuba’s Worst Fuel Crisis in Decades May Get Relief From Russia

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the conflict in the Middle East. On today's show, Former House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Rep. Michael McCaul, J Street Senior Vice President Ilan Goldenberg, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget President Maya MacGuineas. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He's Disappointed in NATO | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/17/2026

author: Chris Strohm, Jimmy Jenkins
description: The House Oversight Committee ordered US Attorney General Pam Bondi to appear for a deposition on the US Justice Department’s handling of the investigation and release of files related to sex trafficking by disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein.
title: Bondi Ordered by House Committee to Testify on Epstein Probe

description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Cuba's economy does not work and "they have to change dramatically." President Donald Trump says something will be done soon. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rubio Says Cuba's Economy Does Not Work

author: Kamil Kowalcze
description: Germany moved to cap how often gas stations can raise prices and tighten antitrust oversight in response to a consumer backlash over war-driven price increases.
title: Germany Curbs Gas Station Hikes, Toughens Antitrust Oversight

author: Martha Viotti Beck
description: Brazil is set for a shakeup at the top of its economic team just months before presidential elections, with a new lineup that will need to signal President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s policy direction through 2027.
title: Lula Revamps Economic Team Ahead of Brazil Elections

author: Daniel Hornak
description: Slovakia’s government repealed a law abolishing the Whistleblower Protection Office after it said the European Union’s executive arm threatened to withhold funds tied to anti-corruption standards.
title: Slovakia Keeps Whistleblower Office After EU Funding Threat

author: Greg Stohr
description: US Chief Justice John Roberts said hostility toward individual Supreme Court members was creating a dangerous environment, in his first public comments since the president blasted justices who voted to strike down his global tariffs.
title: Roberts Slams ‘Dangerous’ Enmity Toward Supreme Court Justices

author: Omar Tamo
description: Iran has stepped up attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent days, signaling it’s targeting the oil-rich kingdom more aggressively than earlier in the war.
title: Iran Ups Attacks on Oil-Rich Saudi Arabia as War Rages On

description: President Donald Trump says he's disappointed in NATO for not doing more to help in the Iran War. He speaks in the Oval Office.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says 'I'm Disappointed in NATO'

author: Catherine Lucey, Josh Wingrove, Hadriana Lowenkron
description: Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin defended British Prime Minister Keir Starmer after the UK leader was criticized by President Donald Trump for not more fully supporting the war on Iran.
title: Irish PM Comes to Starmer’s Defense During White House Visit

description: President Donald Trump says his trip to China for a summit with Xi Jinping will take place and would happen in “about five or six weeks." He spoke at the White House during a sit-down with the Irish prime minister. The trip was postponed because of the war with Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He's 'Resetting' a Meeting With China's Xi

author: Peter Martin, Grant Smith, Weilun Soon
description: US President Donald Trump is desperate to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to ease a growing global energy crisis. He won’t achieve that easily without a ceasefire in the war on Iran.
title: Hormuz Reopening Looks Unlikely Without a Ceasefire in Iran War

description: President Donald Trump reacts to the news that Joe Kent, a top counterterrorism official, was resigning in protest of the war with Iran. Trump said it's a good thing he's out and Kent was "weak on security." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Joe Kent Was Weak on Security

author: Andrea Palasciano, Arne Delfs, Francine Lacqua
description: Europe is learning how to say “no” to Donald Trump over his war in Iran.
title: Europe Stands Up to Donald Trump Threats Over Iran War Support

description: "We don't need help," President Donald Trump says when asked at the White House about NATO allies assisting in the Strait of Hormuz. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says NATO Is Making a 'Very Foolish Mistake'

author: Josh Wingrove, Hadriana Lowenkron
description: US President Donald Trump announced his highly anticipated summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping is being postponed, injecting uncertainty into the two countries’ ongoing trade negotiations.
title: Trump Says He’s Rescheduling Xi Meeting as Iran War Rages On

author: Katrina Manson
description: The Pentagon is working to develop alternatives to Anthropic PBC’s artificial intelligence tools, according to a senior US defense official, following a Trump administration decision to declare the company a supply-chain risk in a feud over safeguards governing military use of the technology.
title: Pentagon Moving to Replace Anthropic Amid AI Feud, Official Says

author: Kamil Kowalcze, Arno Schuetze
description: A senior German official said he’s worried about risks for the country’s economic backbone of small and medium-sized enterprises if Commerzbank AG were to be acquired by UniCredit SpA.
title: Germany Says Commerzbank Takeover Could Curb Mittelstand Loans

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: US President Donald Trump lashed out against longtime allies, many of which have rejected his appeals for help in the Iran War effort, as the closure of a vital waterway continued to wreak havoc on global energy markets.
title: Trump Belittles Allies That Rejected His Iran War Appeals

description: Joe Kent, the director of the National Counterterrorism Center, has resigned over the war with Iran. He says the country posed no threat and he blames Israel for dragging the US into the conflict. Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall reports from the White House.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Top Trump Counterterrorism Official Quits Over Iran War

author: Joe Mayes, Philip Aldrick
description: Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves said she is drawing up plans to give regional leaders in the UK control of some national tax revenues as part of her push to raise economic growth across Britain.
title: Reeves Floats Plan to Give UK Regions Say Over Tax Funds

author: Oscar Medina, Stephan Kueffner
description: Colombia and Ecuador traded accusations over alleged bombing along their chaotic joint border, raising tensions that were already high due to a trade war.
title: Colombia Accuses Ecuador’s Forces of Bombing Across Joint Border

author: Jorge Valero, Max Ramsay
description: The European Union will restart ratification of its trade deal with the US, setting up the long-delayed agreement for final approval.
title: EU to Restart Process to Ratify US Trade Deal After Block

author: Jamie Tarabay, Alicia Diaz, Josh Wingrove
description: A top counterterrorism official and staunch MAGA Republican resigned over the war with Iran, claiming that Israel had misled President Donald Trump into believing that the regime in Tehran posed an imminent threat.
title: Top Counterterrorism Official Resigns in Protest of Iran War

author: Michelle Kaske, Chris Dolmetsch
description: New York’s transit authority sued the Trump administration to unpause federal funds tied to a $7 billion project that would extend the Second Avenue subway to Harlem.
title: NY’s MTA Sues Trump Administration Over Frozen Subway Funds

author: Erin Ailworth, Michael Hirtzer, Skylar Woodhouse, Ilena Peng
description: US farmers, long one of Donald Trump’s most loyal constituencies, are increasingly worried by the Iran war as soaring fertilizer and fuel prices hammer them just as they are about to start planting crops for the year.
title: Iran War Cost Spike Straining Farmers Ahead of Midterm Elections

author: Jim Wyss
description: Donald Trump’s top diplomat said an initial move by Havana to open its economy to the Cuban diaspora fell short, with the island beginning to claw its way out of another national blackout amid intense US pressure.
title: Rubio Faults Cuba’s Exile Outreach as Island Emerges From Blackout

author: Selcan Hacaoglu, Laura Dhillon Kane
description: Canada has no intention of joining offensive military actions against Iran, Foreign Minister Anita Anand told Bloomberg News.
title: Canada Rules Out Joining Offensive Operations Against Iran

author: Nacha Cattan
description: In Roxbury, New Jersey, a suburban township about 40 miles west of New York City, the mayor and the entire town council are Republicans.
title: NJ Town Fights ICE Facility at Warehouse Sold by Goldman Sachs

author: Alaric Nightingale
description: Moldova summoned Russia’s ambassador to complain about Moscow’s strike on a Ukrainian facility that caused a petroleum products spill in the Dniester river and threatened local water supplies.
title: Moldova Summons Russian Envoy as Hit on Ukraine Pollutes Water

description: Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said Greece and Europe will not participate in any military operations near Iran. “The simple answer is no, Greece is not going to participate in any operation around the theater of current operations,” he said at a Bloomberg event in Athens on Tuesday.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Greek PM on Iran Involvement: 'The Simple Answer Is No'

author: Aliaksandr Kudrytski, Marton Kasnyik
description: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban said he’ll continue to block key European Union aid to Ukraine until flows of Russian oil via the Druzhba pipeline are fully restored, despite President Volodymyr Zelenskiy’s decision to allow EU experts into his country to help with repairs.
title: Orban Amps Up Druzhba Oil Standoff After Kyiv Accepts EU Mission

author: Nduka Orjinmo
description: Suicide bombers staged deadly attacks on three crowded locations in the northeastern Nigerian city of Maiduguri, the first coordinated operation of its kind there in almost a decade.
title: Coordinated Suicide Attack in Nigeria Leaves 23 People Dead

author: Sotiris Nikas, Paul Tugwell, Francine Lacqua
description: Greece will soon propose a social media ban for anyone under 15 years old, Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said.
title: Greece Is Preparing Social Media Ban for Children Under 15

author: Skylar Woodhouse
description: The Trump administration has moved to locate backup sources of fertilizers for American farmers at the start of the planting season after the Iran war shut down a key source of supply.
title: War Spurs US Backup Fertilizer Push Before Planting Season

description: Israel said it killed Iran’s security chief, Ali Larijani, in an overnight strike. Defense Minister Israel Katz said Larijani, the secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, was “eliminated” alongside the commander of Iran’s paramilitary Basij unit. Iran is yet to comment on the claim. Bloomberg’s Joumanna Bercetche has the latest.
title: Israel Says Iran Security Chief Larijani Has Been Killed

author: Alan Crawford
description: Such a clear rejection hasn’t been witnessed since Europe refused to bow to demands for control of Greenland.
title: Trump Finds Allies Are Few in Times of War

author: Sotiris Nikas, Paul Tugwell, Francine Lacqua
description: Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said Greece and Europe will not participate in any military operations near Iran, after US President Donald Trump demanded that allies send vessels to help restart shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
title: Mitsotakis Says Europe Won’t Join Military Efforts Near Iran

author: Jen Judson
description: The US Navy and the General Services Administration awarded a contract worth up to $71 million to Gecko Robotics to use its wall-climbing robots to assess the health of naval vessels, the company announced Tuesday.
title: US Navy Awards Contract to Gecko Robotics to Inspect Ships

author: Coulter Jones, Noah Buhayar
description: Debt collectors are blindsiding borrowers with years of back interest on old home loans. States are becoming a flashpoint in the legal battle.
title: ‘Zombie’ Second Mortgages Spur New Battles in State Capitols

description: Iran set a massive natural gas field in the United Arab Emirates ablaze as it steps up attacks on key energy sites. The drone attack on the Shah field, close to the border with Saudi Arabia, marks the first time Iran has damaged an oil or gas upstream facility in the country during the war. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Launches Fresh Attacks on Energy Supplies

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, President Donald Trump has reiterated his appeals for other nations to help secure the Strait of Hormuz, voicing his frustration with those that have been publicly noncommittal.

Meanwhile, Iran stepped up attacks on energy infrastructure, with operations suspended at the Shah natural gas field in the UAE due to a fire, while a drone attack temporarily shut the Fujairah port.

Trump said he asked Beijing to delay his meeting with Xi Jinping for about a month, saying it was important for him to remain in Washington to oversee the Iran war.

Today's guests: Pictet Asset Management Senior Economist Sabrina Khanniche (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War: Trump Demands Help With Hormuz & Trump-Xi Delay Request | Daybreak Europe 3/17/2026

description: The European Union’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said EU foreign ministers on Monday showed “no appetite” to extend the bloc’s maritime security mission to the Strait of Hormuz from the Red Sea. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump reiterated his appeals for other nations to help secure the key oil shipping route. Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook breaks down the situation.
title: EU Shows No Appetite to Change Red Sea Maritime Mandate

author: Kateryna Kadabashy, Dana Khraiche
description: Iran set a massive natural gas field in the United Arab Emirates ablaze as it steps up attacks on key energy sites, while US President Donald Trump appealed to allies and the likes of China to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
title: Iran Hits UAE Gas Field as Trump Pushes Allies to Help on Hormuz

description: US President Donald Trump has reiterated his appeals for other nations to help secure the Strait of Hormuz, saying Iran was nearly obliterated even as the war continues to roil oil markets and global shipping. Torbjorn Soltvedt, Principal Middle East analyst at Verisk Maplecroft spoke to Bloomberg’s Horizons Middle East and Africa anchor Joumanna Bercetche on the war & its impact on the Middle East. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Soltvedt: Iran’s Actions to Maximize Economic Disruption

author: Patpicha Tanakasempipat
description: Thailand will start building fences along a portion of its border with Cambodia next month to boost security after deadly clashes between the countries erupted last year following longstanding tensions.
title: Thailand to Start Building Border Fences After Cambodia Clashes

author: Zoe Schneeweiss, Bastian Benrath-Wright
description: Swiss National Bank President Martin Schlegel received a salary of 986,200 Swiss francs ($1.2 million) in 2025, ensuring he remains one of the world’s best-paid central bank chiefs.
title: SNB President Martin Schlegel’s Salary Is Now $1.2 Million

description: Emergency workers search for people trapped in rubble following a strike on a residential building in Tehran on March 16. Source: Getty Images/Getty Images
title: Iran Continues Attacks on Energy Supplies, Oil Rises

author: Jennifer Duggan, Olivia Fletcher
description: Irish Premier Micheál Martin will gift Donald Trump the traditional bowl of shamrock when he meets the US president for St. Patrick’s Day, part of a charm offensive as the nation seeks to safeguard an economic model built on US investment.
title: Ireland Woos Trump in St. Patrick’s Day Charm Offensive

description: Iran stepped up attacks on energy infrastructure around the Persian Gulf and set a massive gas field ablaze, adding more pressure to an increasingly fraught global fuel supply situation. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports from Dubai on the latest developments. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: UAE Gas Field Set Ablaze as Iran Strikes Continue

author: Brendan Murray
description: The US is pushing to make permanent an international ban on tariffs on ecommerce, setting the stage for a debate on America’s global dominance of digital services and data flows at the World Trade Organization’s ministerial later this month.
title: US Presses WTO to Keep the Global Internet Tariff-Free Forever

author: Weilun Soon, Alex Longley
description: A Pakistani tanker earlier this week became the latest vessel to sail out through the Strait of Hormuz by hewing closely to the Iranian coast, suggesting an approved route that points to Tehran’s tightening grip on the narrow waterway — even as the US seeks to assert control.
title: Hormuz Escape Route Suggests Ships Navigating on Iran’s Terms

author: Alexander Weber, Kamil Kowalcze
description: Fabian Schmitt is seeing a leap in demand from defense clients eager to deploy his aircraft software.
title: Merz’s €600 Billion Defense Push Is Rippling Across Germany

author: Charlie Zhu, Jing Li, Colum Murphy
description: President Donald Trump’s request for a delay to his summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping is a likely welcome development for Beijing, even as it threatens to inject new uncertainty into ties between the world’s two largest economies.
title: Trump’s Delay of Xi Summit Buys China Time to Game Out Iran War

author: Volodymyr Verbianyi, Olesia Safronova
description: The International Monetary Fund raised concern about Ukraine’s ability to continue receiving aid from its $8.1 billion package as lawmakers stall on measures needed to release the financing, its representative said.
title: IMF Raises Alarm Over Aid to Ukraine With Parliament in Gridlock

author: Catherine Lucey
description: President Donald Trump has long used last-minute switches on foreign travel and meetings with heads of state as he seeks to gain a diplomatic upper hand and keep foreign partners on their toes.
title: Trump’s Delay of Xi Visit Echoes Pattern of Last-Minute Changes

author: Sakura Murakami, Akemi Terukina
description: Japan’s defense minister said the US hadn’t made a specific demand to send ships to the Middle East, following media reports that Tokyo has started to explore that possibility ahead of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s summit with US President Donald Trump this week.
title: Japan Stays Guarded on Trump’s Ship Demands Ahead of Summit

author: Claire Jiao
description: Afghanistan accused Pakistan of launching an airstrike that killed at least 400 people at a drug treatment hospital, in what could mark a major escalation in fighting between the neighbors.
title: Afghanistan Says 400 Killed in Pakistan Airstrike on Kabul Hospital

author: Soo-Hyang Choi
description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged South Korea, a major oil importer, to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, doubling down on President Donald Trump’s drive to coax security allies into helping America secure the key waterway.
title: Rubio Urges Korea to Back Hormuz Efforts as Trump Ups Pressure
